full_judgment: 2. The short fact is that the respondents as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.42 of 1983 before the teamed Assistant Judge, Fenchugonj, Sylhet against the petitioners as defendants praying for declaration of title, recovery of khas possession in 1st and 2nd schedule land and for confirmation of possession in the 3rd schedule land alleging, inter alia, that the land as described in 1st, 2nd and 3rd schedule of the plaint belonged to two brothers, Md. Anis and Md. Torab in 8 annas share and Bans and at the time of marriage a portion of the suit land was transferred to the said Nasira Banu in lieu of dower. After the said marriage, said Nasira Banu was owning and possessing a portion of the 1st 2nd and 3rd schedule lands on the basis of the transfer in lieu of dower through a kabala which was executed about 100 years back. Then Md. Torab died leaving behind his widow Nasira Banu and two sons Abdullah and Abdur Rab as heirs. On the death of Anis his share devolved upon his brother's sons Abdullah and Abdur Rab. Abdullah and Abdur Rab died during their childhood and their mother Nasira Banu became owner and possessor of 1st 2nd and 3rd schedule lands. The said Nasira Banu brought her brother's daughters, Aziza Khatun, Abeja Khatun and Sharifa Khatun and brought them up in her house and subsequently Nasira Banu got married Aziza Khatun to one of his relations Md. Aminuddin Chowdhury and brought them to her house and transferred some portion of land from the 1st, 2nd and 3rd schedule by registered deed of Hebanama dated 15th Sraban 1306 B.S. and put them in possession. Subsequently, before her death Nasira Banu made oral gift of her remaining share in the suit land in favour of the parents of the plaintiffs and put them in possession and accordingly the plaintiffs' parents became owner in possession of the suit land and subsequently they died leaving behind the plaintiffs. Subsequently in the First part of Agrahayan, 1378 B.S. the defendant No.1 along with his brother and other defendants took away the ripe paddy from 2nd and 3rd schedule land and accordingly dispossessed the plaintiffs there from., On enquiry the plaintiff learnt that the defendant No.1 got the 1st and 2nd schedule that Md. Torab was married to one Nasira land wrongly recorded, which is absolutely without any basis. The plaintiffs have been in possession of the 3rd schedule land.
